findings.title: Guard the missing destination calendar in the Meet fallback
findings.body: When an event uses Google Meet but has no destination calendar, destructuring produces an undefined mainHostDestinationCalendar and accessing its integration throws. Previously the optional access allowed this case to fall back to Cal Video. Booking creation now fails instead of using that fallback.

findings.title: Pass the current destination to non-Google calendar adapters
findings.body: Each destination's credential is used to create an event, but every adapter receives the full destination array. Office365CalendarService, LarkCalendarService, and BaseCalendarService always select the first entry rather than the entry for that credential. In a collective booking, secondary hosts therefore attempt to write to the primary host's calendar ID, which can fail authorization; CalDAV can also silently create nothing because no listed calendar matches. Scope the event's destination to the current destination or make all adapters select by credential ID.

findings.title: Retain secondary host calendars when the organizer has none
findings.body: The destinationCalendar field is initialized to null if neither the event type nor organizer has a destination calendar. The optional push then discards all collected secondary-host destinations. A collective event whose main host has no calendar but whose other hosts have connected calendars consequently creates no calendar events for those hosts. Initialize an empty array before appending the team destinations.

findings.title: Preserve credential IDs on video references
findings.body: Reference creation now sets credentialId to undefined for every non-calendar result, dropping the credential ID returned by createVideoEvent. Cancellation only deletes a video meeting when its booking reference has a credentialId, so newly created Zoom and other video meetings will no longer be deleted when their bookings are cancelled. Preserve result.credentialId for video results as before.

findings.title: Restore the destination fallback for legacy Google references
findings.body: When externalCalendarId is null or absent, the new fallback searches destination calendars for an externalId equal to that missing value, which cannot match a normal calendar ID. Google update requests consequently receive no calendarId and fail for legacy booking references without a stored external calendar ID, even when the event has a valid destination calendar. The analogous delete fallback instead targets primary and can leave events in non-primary calendars undeleted.

findings.title: Delete recurring instances using each reference's own credential
findings.body: In the all-remaining-recurring-bookings branch, the fetched credential for the current reference is ignored. The code instead iterates only the organizer's credentials and selects just the first calendar reference from each instance. For the newly supported collective bookings, secondary hosts' calendar events are never deleted, even though every booking is marked cancelled. Iterate the references of each updated booking and resolve their matching credentials.

findings.title: Do not reverse organization slug assignment
findings.body: This changes slug assignment from when team billing is disabled to when it is enabled. With billing disabled, newly created organizations now receive neither a slug nor a requestedSlug, despite the requested subdomain being configured above. With billing enabled, the slug is assigned immediately instead of remaining a requested slug. Restore the original condition so organization routing and the billing-gated slug workflow retain their existing behavior.
